title: OpenAPI specs do not include security scheme documentation
description: The OpenAPI specifications returned by the platform do not include security scheme definitions, making it impossible for agents to discover authentication requirements programmatically.
reproduction_steps: Download the OpenAPI spec for any API using 'jentic apis spec <api-ref>'
Examine the spec for security schemes or authentication requirements
Observe that no security information is present
expected_behavior: OpenAPI specs should include security scheme definitions (e.g., apiKey, bearer, oauth2) that document how to authenticate with the API.
actual_behavior: OpenAPI specs lack security scheme documentation, forcing users to discover authentication requirements through out-of-band channels.
evidence: [docs] task=read-api-spec | Agent noted OpenAPI specs lack security scheme documentation, making auth requirements undiscoverable
**2. Authentication Documentation Gap** (Significant discoverability issue) - OpenAPI specs don't document security schemes

title: Missing CLI command for OAuth metadata discovery
description: The CLI does not provide a command to fetch OAuth authorization server metadata, forcing users to make manual HTTP requests.
reproduction_steps: Attempt to discover OAuth metadata using CLI commands
Find no 'jentic oauth' or similar command exists
Resort to manual curl request to /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
expected_behavior: CLI should provide a command like 'jentic oauth metadata' to fetch OAuth authorization server metadata.
actual_behavior: No CLI command exists; users must use curl or other HTTP clients.
evidence: [AX] task=discover-oauth-metadata | No CLI command for OAuth metadata discovery; agent resorted to manual curl
**1. CLI Coverage Gaps** (Major UX issue) - No `jentic oauth metadata` - had to use curl for OAuth discovery

title: Missing CLI command for viewing audit events
description: The CLI does not provide a command to list or query audit events, forcing users to make manual API requests.
reproduction_steps: Attempt to list audit events using CLI commands
Find no 'jentic events list' or similar command exists
Resort to manual curl request to /events endpoint
expected_behavior: CLI should provide a command like 'jentic events list' to query audit events.
actual_behavior: No CLI command exists; users must use curl or other HTTP clients to access the REST API directly.
evidence: [AX] task=view-audit-events | No 'jentic events list' CLI command; agent used curl to access audit log
**1. CLI Coverage Gaps** (Major UX issue) - No `jentic events list` - had to use curl for audit/event logs

title: No broker dry-run or preview capability available
description: The platform does not provide a way to preview or dry-run broker execution before actually making the proxied request.
reproduction_steps: Attempt to preview a broker execution using 'jentic execute --dry-run' or similar
Attempt to use the /inspect endpoint for broker preview
Find no documented or working method for broker dry-run
expected_behavior: Platform should provide a way to preview what a broker call would do without executing it (e.g., --dry-run flag or inspect endpoint support).
actual_behavior: No dry-run or preview capability is available for broker executions.
evidence: [docs] task=inspect-before-execute | Agent tried control plane inspect endpoint directly but found no broker dry-run capability; concluded feature is missing
**3. Missing Broker Inspection** (Documentation gap) - No documented way to dry-run/preview broker behavior before execution
